facts.text: UR5Controller imports MoveJoints and MoveTo from ros_impedance_controller.srv.
UR5Controller imports generic_float from ros_impedance_controller.srv.
UR5Controller registers the absolute service /ur5/move_joints with the MoveJoints type.
UR5Controller registers the absolute service /ur5/move_to with the MoveTo type.
UR5Controller registers the absolute service /ur5/move_gripper with the generic_float type.
MoveJoints.srv declares request fields dt, v_des and q_des and response field bool success.
MoveTo.srv declares request fields pose_target, dt and v_des and response field bool success.
generic_float.srv declares request field data and response field bool ack.
The move_joints callback gets a MoveIt trajectory and calls move_joints for every trajectory point, returning False when planning fails and True after the loop.
The move_joints loop advances q_des by dt * v_ref * e / ||e|| and stops only when ||e|| is below 0.001; the loop has no cancellation, deadline or operator-stop check.

The move_gripper callback creates ros.Rate(1/self.dt), then loops, sending the arm reference and sleeping on the rate, until any filtered desired gripper joint is within 0.0001 of the target; a TODO to handle a timeout follows the loop.
move_joints creates ros.Rate(1/dt) and sleeps on it in every loop iteration.
UR5Controller creates ServiceProxy objects for /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/unpause_physics with the std_srvs/Empty type.
UR5Controller imports Empty from std_srvs.srv.
UR5Controller subscribes to /ur5/joint_states with the JointState type.
UR5Controller imports JointState from sensor_msgs.msg.
UR5Controller publishes /ur5/ee_pose with the geometry_msgs.msg.Pose type.
The configured arm joint order is shoulder_pan_joint, shoulder_lift_joint, elbow_joint, wrist_1_joint, wrist_2_joint, wrist_3_joint.
The UR5e joint_limit_params file states per-joint min_position and max_position for the six arm joints: [-6.14, 6.14], [-3.14, 0], [-3.14, 3.14], [-6.28, 6.28], [-6.28, 6.28], [-6.28, 6.28].
The configured control period dt is 0.001 s.
The simulated motion client sets v_des to 0.6.
The controller's simulated v_des branch sets 0.6; the real-robot branch sets 0.2.
ros_impedance_controller_ur5.launch includes gazebo_ros empty_world.launch with paused default true and use_sim_time default true.
ros_impedance_controller_ur5.launch defaults joint_limit_params to the ur5e joint_limits.yaml.
The shipped UR5 parameters set real_robot to False.
startRealRobot kills rviz, gzserver and gzclient, logs STARTING REAL ROBOT and exits unless the ROS master is online and '/' + robot_name + '/ur_hardware_interface' is a running node.
For the real robot the gripper manager opens a TCP socket to 192.168.0.100 port 30002 to send a gripper script; for the simulated robot it only sets the desired finger joints.

The upstream motion client in motion/main.py creates service clients for /ur5/move_joints, /ur5/move_to and /ur5/move_gripper, after waiting for /ur5/move_joints, /ur5/move_to and the relative move_gripper.

determinism.notes: Event-driven contract fake with no physics step, controller, MoveIt planner or wall-clock pacing; placeholder observations do not establish trajectory replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic transport: it answers the declared topics and services with canned values and runs no Gazebo, MoveIt, ros_impedance_controller, physics, contacts or wall-clock loop
joint positions, end-effector pose, gripper state and service acknowledgements are placeholder test data; they do not prove motion, arrival, grasp or stopped state
the fake's /gazebo/pause_physics handler flips a local flag; it does not pause a simulator, does not cancel a pending motion service callback and provides no stopped-state measurement

the clone declares /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/unpause_physics but contains no call to either proxy; mhs.safety.reset does not unpause (SAFE-042), only the explicit resume command does, and live pause semantics must be confirmed against the operator's Gazebo

while Gazebo is paused, every /ur5/move_joints and /ur5/move_gripper callback waits in its simulated-time rate.sleep() (the shipped launch sets use_sim_time) and answers only after a resume or the binding timeout; the fake answers at once and does not model that wait; after a resume an interrupted callback continues its old motion, because the loops have no cancellation, and overlapping calls from several clients all write the shared q_des
the shipped launch starts Gazebo paused and nothing in the clone's main path unpauses it
the upstream motion client (motion/main.py) calls the same motion services; running it beside MHS adds a second commander that the MHS latch does not fence

with real_robot set in params.py the same node drives a real UR5 through ur_robot_driver and sends gripper scripts to 192.168.0.100:30002; no Gazebo exists there, so the e-stop fails SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held and nothing upstream stops the arm

the service callbacks return bare True/False values while the .srv files declare response objects; a live ROS deployment must confirm the serialized service response before relying on the acknowledgement
the fake always answers /ur5/joint_states and /ur5/ee_pose; a paused live topic may go silent, so these are explicit observations, not an automatic resource snapshot

the package exposes /ur5/move_joints, /ur5/move_gripper, /ur5/joint_states, /ur5/ee_pose, /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/unpause_physics only; /ur5/move_to, the ZED camera topics, MoveIt planning, force/torque and the other Gazebo model services are NOT COVERED
a live /ur5/joint_states may include additional gripper joints; the observation returns the published arrays unfiltered and the fake's six-element arrays are placeholders
no real ROS graph, Gazebo, MoveIt, simulator or hardware was contacted; evidence is F0 contract_checked only

operator_required.reason: the clone maps a diameter through atan2(0.5 * (diameter - 40), 60) but states no mechanical opening or closing bound; the operator must supply the reviewed gripper envelope

safe_state.description: Gazebo physics paused by the acknowledged /gazebo/pause_physics service: the simulated arm and its controller freeze, and a running /ur5/move_joints or /ur5/move_gripper callback is held in its simulated-time rate.sleep(), not cancelled; nothing senses quiescence. mhs.safety.reset clears only the latch and leaves Gazebo paused; the explicit resume command unpauses it, and an interrupted motion then continues. With real_robot set there is no Gazebo and this stop fails.
